answer_1.quote: Our framework for natural language watermarking is composed of two phases. Phase 1 is obtaining state S from the text X (or Xwm) using some function g1. Phase 2 comprises function g2 that takes X and S as inputs to generate the valid watermarked texts.

answer_2.quote: We also measure the quality of the watermarked text by comparing it with the original cover text. Following Yang et al. (2022); Abdelnabi and Fritz (2021), we compute the entailment score (ES) using an NLI model (RoBERTa-Large-NLI) and semantic similarity (SS) by comparing the cosine similarity of the representations outputted by a pre-trained sentence transformer (stsb-RoBERTa-base-v2).

answer_4.quote: We also conduct human evaluation comparing the fluency of the watermarked text and cover text (Fluency∆) and how much semantics is maintained (Semantic Similarity; SS) compared to the original cover text in Tab. 5.
answer_4.guideline: Part 1 consisted of rating the fluency of each sentence including the original cover text. Part 2 consisted of rating how much semantics is maintained given the reference sentence (cover text).
